article:
The product should be able to write

Email is how a quiet app proves it exists when nobody has the tab open. “Your order is in.” “Here is the link.” “You left a mark.” That is product email. A newsletter is a different animal and can wait.

To send from you@yourdomain you have to prove the domain — DNS again. SPF, DKIM, DMARC look like runes. They are just notes that say “yes, this server may speak as this name.” Follow the provider’s copy-paste. Do not freelance the records.

Who sends it

Resend, Postmark, Amazon SES, the email product you already pay for. Pick one. Grok can write the template. It cannot warm a domain for you. That is paperwork and patience.

Open Mailer is the later, stranger version of this chapter: one mailbox, many domains, reply from the address that was written to. You do not start there. You start with one from-address that delivers.

How I actually do it

hello@bohobond.com is a door, not a platform. Send Reorder will send the dull, useful kind of mail — the usual order, when a location goes quiet. If that mail lands in spam, the product is broken even if the code is pretty.

Where noobs get stuck

Sending from a Gmail address “just for now” and looking like a phish. Building a newsletter before anyone asked. Or touching nameservers to fix mail and taking the website down with it.

Film this

A single transactional email in a real inbox. Show the from-line. Show it is not the promotions tab. Then show the three DNS notes without pretending you memorised them.

Do this before chapter 14

  • Send one email from the domain, to yourself.
  • Confirm it was not spam.
  • Keep newsletters in a drawer until ten people ask.

Next: APIs and webhooks — your app talks out, other apps talk back.
